simple.meaning: כַּפְתֹּרִי (Kaphtôrîy) is a Hebrew word meaning “a Caphtorite (collectively) or native of Caphtor.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: כַּפְתֹּרִי (H3732) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Genesis 10:14, with occurrences in Genesis, Deuteronomy, 1 Chronicles.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to כַּפְתֹּרִי (H3732) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in כַּפְתֹּרִי (H3732) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: כַּפְתֹּרִי (Kaphtôrîy) / H3732 is traced through Genesis 10:14, Deuteronomy 2:23, 1 Chronicles 1:12 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: a Caphtorite (collectively) or native of Caphtor
definitions.full: H3732. Kaphtori [ כַּפְתֹּרִי ] adjective, of a people , only plural as substantive כַּפְתֹּרִים Cretans ; Gen 10:14 (J) = 1Chr 1:12 ; as expellers of the 'Awwim' from their homes about Gaza, Deut 2:23 . I. כַּר basket-saddle , see below כור .

occurrences.englishText: Pathrusim, Casluhim (which the Philistines descended from), and Caphtorim.
Then the Avvim, who lived in villages as far as Gaza: the Caphtorim, who came out of Caphtor, destroyed them and lived in their place.)
Pathrusim, Casluhim (where the Philistines came from), and Caphtorim.
